Switzerland can stay outside the EU because it sits in the middle of Europe. It borders Germany, France, Italy, and Austria. It has several rich markets within driving distance and still pays for EU access without joining.

Canada does not. It is a country of 40 million, and most of that population lives within 150 miles of the U.S. border. There is one real market next door, not four.

If Washington implements the September 29 bans on a handful of Canadian goods, the pain compounds fast. Canada cannot land a counterblow equal to what the United States can still do to the rest of the trade ledger.

This ends one way. Canada cannot take on an economy 13 times its size and avoid serious capital flight. The damage from the moves both sides are making will take years to show up in full. Capitulation is the destination, not Brussels, where Canada would still have to pay for access. The U.S. terms already on the table will prove the more lucrative offer. Every delay until the deal is finalized only costs Canadians more.

text:
Rate Hike Lands: Relief Rally or Full Reversal? A Roundup of Crypto KOL Market Views 📈

In the early hours of last night, the first rate hike of Warsh’s tenure finally landed: the federal funds rate was raised by 25 bps to 3.75%–4.00%. The dot plot leaned hawkish, pushing up the probability of another hike before year-end.

Just one day earlier, the CLARITY Act failed to secure the required 60 votes and remained stalled. Meanwhile, Japan is highly likely to raise rates by another 25 bps on Friday, while the Strait of Hormuz continues to keep oil prices and inflation under pressure.

Under the old playbook, the crypto market should have taken a sharp dive. Instead, BTC has continued to trade around $75,000–$76,000, many altcoins have rallied, and ZEC has even reached another all-time high.

So where does the market go from here?

📈 The Bulls: The Rate Hike Has Been Offset, and the Bad News Is Already Priced In

1️⃣ CZ

@cz_binance

XHunt Global Ranking: 4

Call: Every dip is an opportunity.

View: CZ offered no qualifications. During rate-hike week, this statement itself reflects his positioning: treat pullbacks as opportunities to accumulate more, rather than pessimistically assuming the trend is over.

2️⃣ Arthur Hayes

@CryptoHayes

XHunt Global Ranking: 14

Call: In a high-debt environment, rate hikes can actually be stimulative; financial assets will continue to rise.

View: Hayes believes that when government debt is high enough, rate hikes increase interest paid on bank reserves and coupon income for T-bill holders. The net effect is more spending, particularly on financial assets.

The Fed ended RMP in mid-August, but banks have continued expanding their balance sheets. The combined assets of the Federal Reserve and commercial banks are still growing, effectively creating more money. The price of money is rising, but so is its quantity—meaning risk assets do not necessarily have to follow the old monetary-tightening playbook.

3️⃣ Bitcoin Orange

@oragnes

XHunt Global Ranking: 3090

Call: The worst is already behind us. The expected plunge never came, but the liftoff did.

View: The crypto market has shown remarkable resilience. The CLARITY vote failed 49–50, and rates rose by 25 bps. According to the usual script, the market should have plunged. Instead, ZEC continued to hit new all-time highs after the negative news, while PONS, STONK, ZCAT, and MarsCoin all stabilized and rebounded.

The next catalyst is not another congressional vote, but administrative measures from the SEC and CFTC that could substitute for the CLARITY Act. Hold onto your positions—the opportunities are on-chain.

4️⃣ CryptoPainter

@CryptoPainter

XHunt Global Ranking: 2045

Call: The market was more afraid of “no rate hike.” A hike proves that the Federal Reserve remains independent.

View: Before the decision, CryptoPainter argued that the world was watching the bond market, not the old liquidity narrative. A rate hike would demonstrate that the Fed remains independent, preserve the credibility anchor of the US dollar, and prevent long-term yields from necessarily surging.

After the decision, neither BTC nor US equities collapsed, while long-term yields rebounded only slightly—validating this framework. BTC is still battling around $75,000–$76,000, with a deep negative premium. If that range breaks, he will resume dollar-cost averaging. His strategy has turned bearish, but he has opened only 25% of his intended position because the technical structure has not yet broken down.

⚖️ The Technical Camp: A Short-Term Rebound Is Possible, but Don’t Front-Run the Medium-Term Move

1️⃣ K-Line Cult Leader

@Paris13Jeanne

XHunt Global Ranking: 1891

Call: Rate-hike expectations were priced in ahead of time, but it is still too early to buy the dip at $76,000.

View: BTC has support around $76,000 and could see a short-term rebound. However, the correction on the three-day timeframe is not yet over.

2️⃣ TraderS | Unscrupulous Taoist
@TraderS18

XHunt Global Ranking: 4007

Call: The September rate hike was the key theme he had already identified in late July. The ideal scenario is “rate hike completed + oil prices falling,” which would finally give risk assets some breathing room. Gold is currently a better entry than BTC.

View: Oil prices are the ultimate boss for risk assets. If the Strait of Hormuz situation moves toward a compromise involving accommodation and concessions, causing a structural decline in oil prices, the damage from the rate hike could be offset.

👀 The Cautious Camp: The Hawkish Cycle Isn’t Over, and Japan’s Friday Rate Hike Could Be the Next Blow

1️⃣ Phyrex Ni

@PhyrexNi

XHunt Global Ranking: 736

Call: The Fed’s hammer has fallen, but it is not over yet. High interest rates and the risks surrounding the Strait of Hormuz may coexist for an extended period.

View: The Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 bps, and the dot plot suggests a meaningful probability of another hike in October. Japan is also highly likely to raise rates by 25 bps on Friday.

Even if Trump pulls another TACO in the short term, it would not resolve the Strait of Hormuz issue. Rate hikes and elevated interest rates could therefore persist for a long time.

Phyrex Ni originally planned to place a BTC bid at $72,000. However, realizing that the position would have to weather Japan’s Friday rate decision, he chose not to buy yet. He plans to wait until Japan has completed its hike and market sentiment has stabilized.

2️⃣ Ziqi（Reborn Edition）

@cloakmk

XHunt Global Ranking: 3138

Call: A 25 bps hike itself is not frightening. The real risks are “another hike before year-end” and “higher rates staying in place for longer.” The short-term outlook is range-bound with a bearish bias, while the medium-term direction depends on whether $72,400 holds.

View: His key observation is that “the market did not fall on bad news.” Under the old playbook, a rate hike, a hawkish dot plot, the stalled CLARITY Act, and ETF outflows should have sent BTC toward $70,000. Instead, it fell only to around $75,000 before buyers stepped in.

That means buyers are waiting below, but there is still no one chasing prices higher—so it is too early to declare that the bull market is back.

If BTC climbs above $82,000, the negative catalysts will have largely been priced in. If it falls below $72,400, the decline will simply have arrived late.

text:
Walked away from a $655K self-storage deal after 4 months of diligence.

Here's what happened:

97 units in rural Minnesota. 5 commercial flex bays anchoring 44% of revenue. Rents 20-33% below market on every unit size. Only facility within a mile.

I negotiated a seller carry note: 
0% Year 1, 2% Year 2, 3% Year 3. 
$327k down, $327k carried. 

On paper: 18% cash-on-cash out of the gate with zero debt service for 12 months.

Then the Phase I flagged 20+ years of auto repair operations in the commercial bays. Waste oil drums on cracked concrete. No containment.

Phase II came back with clean soil, clean groundwater - but a PCE vapor exceedance in one sub-slab sample. 4x over the MPCA screening threshold.

Remediation scope: demo and replace the slab, install a sub-slab depressurization system, enroll in the state VIC program, record an environmental covenant on the deed. Permanently. 

$66K all-in. Seller offered $15K credit.

I could have lived with $51K out of pocket. What I couldn't live with was what I learned when I called MPCA directly instead of relying on the consultant's summary.

The covenant runs with the land forever. 

The mitigation fan runs forever. There is maintenance involved. 

Tenant can no longer use their chemicals; which would leave me with 2 vacant flex bays. 

MPCA can revoke closure if additional sampling shows problems. 

MCPA could make me sample and mitigate the entire property, not just the flex bay at any time. 

Every future lender and buyer will see it. 

And the auto shop tenants generating the vapor had no leases, no insurance, and no indemnity running to me.

Great deal structure can't fix open-ended regulatory tail risk.

I spent 20k or so, Phase I and II, survey, and legal to find that out. Worth every dollar.

Hate not closing on a deal I’m in contract on. Rarely ever happens. But for this particular one the risk just wasn’t justified.

text:
The Hanoi Rat Massacre (1902): French colonial authorities in Vietnam offered a bounty for every rat killed, requiring only the tail as proof. People caught rats, cut off their tails to collect the cash, and released the tailless rats so they could breed and yield more bounties.

Corporate Software Development: A tech executive offered engineers a cash bonus for every bug found and fixed. Engineers wrote buggy code in the morning and fixed it in the afternoon to farm the bonuses.

Recycling Subsidies: Subsidizing hazardous e-waste disposal without origin verification led unscrupulous logistics firms to illegally import trash from neighboring regions to claim government cleanup funds.

Anticipate Second-Order Gaming: When designing a reward or KPI, don't just ask "What behavior does this encourage?" Ask "How would an opportunistic actor game this system to collect the reward without solving the underlying problem?"

Reward Outcomes, Not Proxies: Avoid paying people for the volume of effort spent fighting a problem. Align incentives with permanent, systemic resolution metrics that cannot be artificially farmed.

When you pay people to fight fires, don't be surprised when they start carrying matches.

"I beat them 63 to 6." Hear what that sentence contains. Not I built something. Not I discovered something. I won the right to command the men who did.

Notice which man in this story actually holds power. The tech lord can offer you a product you are free to refuse. The congressman can take a share of your earnings before you see it, write the rules under which you may work, and send armed men if you decline. He calls the first one a lord and himself the people.

Rand identified the distinction precisely. Power over nature ends at matter and requires no one's obedience. Power over men requires men, which is why the power-luster can never be finished and can never work alone.

And he needs them to be lords. If they are just men who are good at building things, then beating them in a vote means nothing. So the villain gets invented first, and the ruling comes after.

He did not build the industry. He won a vote about who gets to run it.

text:
Hyperscalers’ pivot to Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) exposes a brutal mismatch: AI compute scales on an 18-month cycle, while nuclear capital and gigawatt-scale grid interconnections operate on a decadal clock.

云巨头对小型模块化核反应堆（SMR）的押注暴露了残酷的周期错配：AI算力以18个月为周期指数演进，而核能资本与吉瓦级电网互联工程的交付却深陷长达十年的物理与监管长周期。

Despite aggressive tech PPAs, SMRs face brutal First-of-a-Kind (FOAK) CAPEX inflation, HALEU enrichment bottlenecks, and protracted NRC licensing queues. Commercial modular baseload power cannot reliably inject multi-GW electrons into data centers before 2032, making legacy reactor life-extensions the only pragmatic bridge.

尽管早期购电协议频出，SMR仍面临首堆建造成本失控、高丰度低浓缩铀（HALEU）供应链短缺及漫长的核管会认证。小型反应堆无法在2032年前向数据中心交付吉瓦级基荷电力，现役成熟核电机组延寿是中短期唯一的物理解法。

Concurrently, transmission queues across key US ISOs like PJM now stretch beyond six years for high-voltage substations. While "behind-the-meter" co-location offers a tactical detour, it triggers severe FERC regulatory pushback over transmission cost-shifting and retail ratepayer subsidization.

与此同时，PJM等核心电网的吉瓦级高压变电接入排队已拉长至六年以上。尽管巨头试图通过“表后直连”现役核电绕过并网审查，但这已引爆联邦能源监管委员会（FERC）对输电成本外溢与民用电价补贴的强力监管阻击。

The defining moat in sovereign-scale AI compute has shifted from silicon FLOPS/Watt to the velocity of securing regulatory-cleared, thermodynamic baseload power.

决定顶级AI算力扩张的终极壁垒，已彻底从芯片层面的算力能效比，转向突破刚性电网监管、兑现热力学吉瓦级基荷电力的工程速度。

text:
Generac surged 18% after landing an Amazon data-center generator agreement with $2.4B of initial deliveries and purchase-linked warrants that can vest on up to $8B of spending. 

The Nasdaq jumped 1.69% as oil and Treasury yields eased; crypto stocks also rebounded after the SEC unveiled a five-year exemption for tokenized-stock trading. 

Meanwhile, CoreWeave fell 4.2% after launching $3B of convertible debt plus a potential 35M-share ATM, while Fluence plunged 15.4% after cutting FY2026 revenue guidance.

Everything that mattered in the market today:

👉 COMPANIES

1. $GNRC/$AMZN: Generac closed up about 18% after Amazon agreed to $2.4B of initial backup-generator deliveries for 2027-28; Amazon also received warrants for up to 1.69M GNRC shares, with additional vesting tied to purchases that can reach $8B.

2. $ARM: Arm jumped about 8.6% after CEO Rene Haas said the chip designer is increasingly confident in its $2B AI-chip sales target, with demand strong enough that supply is the main constraint.

3. $NOK/$MSFT: Nokia rose roughly 4.5%-6% after expanding its Microsoft partnership to combine Nokia Data Suite with Microsoft Fabric for agentic, AI-driven telecom network automation.

4. $LCID/$NVDA: Lucid rose about 5.9% after partnering with Bolt to target at least 25,000 Level 4 autonomous vehicles in Europe using Lucid's midsize platform and Nvidia Hyperion technology.

5. $NKE: Nike's Dow position came under fresh scrutiny as Reuters noted the stock is now the index's smallest weight at about 0.4% and is being removed from the S&P 100 after an 80% market-value decline over five years.

6. $GE: GE Aerospace said its $11.75B acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products is a targeted response to castings bottlenecks, not a blueprint for broad vertical integration; GEnx deliveries rose 50% y/y in Q2.

7. CRUSOE/NVDA: Private AI-infrastructure provider Crusoe raised $3.9B at a $30.9B post-money valuation; Nvidia joined the round, while Crusoe disclosed more than $140B of contracted value and over 6 GW of contracted capacity.

👉 EARNINGS / GUIDANCE

8. $LEN: Lennar reported Q3 EPS of $1.19 on roughly $8.0B revenue, below consensus; homebuilding gross margin fell to 15.8% from 17.5% a year earlier as incentives protected volume.

9. $FLNC: Fluence Energy plunged 15.4% after cutting FY2026 revenue guidance to about $2.4B from roughly $3.0B and widening its adjusted EBITDA loss outlook to about $200M, citing Houston manufacturing delays.

10. $NUE: Nucor guided Q3 EPS to $5.55-$5.65 and said it repurchased about 2.03M shares at an average $247.04 during the quarter.

👉 ANALYST ACTIONS

11. $JBHT: Citizens upgraded J.B. Hunt to Outperform from Market Perform with a $300 target, arguing the roughly 18% pullback since Q2 earnings improved risk/reward.

12. $TCOM: Macquarie upgraded https://t.co/lBoBQ8vnKi to Outperform from Neutral and raised its target to $53.20 from $44.30.

13. $LYFT: Lyft was downgraded in Thursday's Wall Street research slate as analysts reassessed ride-hailing valuation and competitive expectations.

14. $ZS: Bernstein remained bullish on Zscaler and raised its target to $298, while taking a more cautious stance on several cybersecurity peers.

15. $PANW/$OKTA/$S: Bernstein downgraded Palo Alto Networks, Okta and SentinelOne to Market Perform, warning that AI-driven cybersecurity enthusiasm has pushed valuations ahead of fundamentals.

16. $FLNC: Goldman Sachs downgraded Fluence to Neutral from Buy with a $9 target; Piper Sandler cut its target to $5 as execution problems overwhelmed strong storage demand.

👉 M&A / CAPITAL MOVES

17. $CRWV: CoreWeave fell 4.2% after launching a $3B convertible-note sale with a $500M option plus an ATM program for up to 35M shares; at Wednesday's close the ATM could raise roughly $2.9B.

18. $HPK: Permian producer HighPeak Energy is exploring a sale after receiving acquisition interest; it has about $1B of equity value, $1.1B of long-term debt and produced roughly 45,500 boe/day in H1.

19. BROOKFIELD/ACME: Brookfield agreed to invest up to $600M in India's ACME Cleantech Ventures to develop green-ammonia and green-methanol projects.

20. $SVM: Silvercorp renewed a buyback authorization for up to 8.85M shares, roughly 4% of shares outstanding, running from September 21, 2026 through September 20, 2027.

21. $DOMH: Dominari Holdings authorized a share-repurchase program of up to $5M.

👉 REGULATION / LEGAL

22. $COIN/$HOOD/$CRCL: Coinbase and Circle each rose 5.8% and Robinhood gained 5.2% after the SEC unveiled a five-year exemption allowing qualifying platforms to offer tokenized-stock trading without full exchange registration.

23. SEC TOKENIZATION: The SEC framework also grants liquidity providers a five-year dealer-registration exemption, requires tokenized shares to preserve traditional voting and dividend rights, and excludes synthetic stock tokens.

24. $BABA/ANTHROPIC: Reuters reported a U.S. government website used an Alibaba AI search model despite FBI allegations that the model's developer copied Anthropic technology, adding another policy flashpoint around Chinese AI systems.

👉 FDA / BIOTECH

25. RARE: Ultragenyx gained more than 10% after the FDA approved Fayuvi, the first treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome Type A; the one-time gene therapy is expected to reach specialized U.S. centers within 30-60 days.

26. NUVB: Nuvation Bio advanced after the FDA approved an Ibtrozi label update incorporating new mid-stage trial data for the company's cancer therapy.

👉 DIVIDENDS / SHAREHOLDER RETURNS

27. FAF: First American Financial raised its quarterly dividend 11% to $0.61 per share, payable October 5 to holders of record September 28.

28. SVM: Silvercorp's renewed NCIB permits repurchases of up to 4% of outstanding shares; all repurchased shares will be cancelled.

👉 MARKET THEMES

29. SPY/QQQ/DIA: The Dow rose 0.62% to 51,779.85, the S&P 500 gained 1.14% to 7,637.74 and the Nasdaq jumped 1.69% to 26,418.30 in a broad post-Fed rebound.

30. TECH: Technology led all 11 S&P 500 sectors as falling long-term yields revived demand for duration-sensitive growth stocks.

31. SOX/XAU: Semiconductors and gold/silver miners each advanced more than 3%, among the session's strongest industry groups.

32. TREASURIES: The 10-year Treasury yield fell back below 5% toward roughly 4.93%-4.95%, easing a major valuation headwind for equities.

33. OIL: Crude touched a one-week low as reports of Saudi supply moving through Oman eased immediate disruption fears, though Middle East risks kept oil above pre-war levels.

34. LABOR: Initial jobless claims fell to 196,000, the lowest since mid-July, reinforcing the Fed's view that the labor market can absorb tighter policy.

35. HOUSING: Single-family housing starts rose 7.6% in August, but permits fell 1.8% and mortgage rates approached 7%, leaving the sector caught between supply improvement and affordability pressure.

36. FED: Markets priced about a 53.1% probability of another 25-bp Fed hike in October, up sharply from 27.2% a week earlier.

37. BREADTH: NYSE advancers beat decliners 2.38-to-1 and Nasdaq advancers 2.21-to-1, a sharp reversal from Wednesday's weak internals.

38. VOLUME: U.S. exchange volume reached 17.57B shares versus a 20-day average of 15.37B, showing the rebound carried above-normal participation.

👉 STOCKS TO WATCH

39. GNRC/AMZN: The Amazon contract materially changes Generac's data-center revenue visibility; investors will now watch capacity expansion and whether purchase-linked warrants signal follow-on hyperscaler volume.

40. CRWV: CoreWeave's financing package puts dilution, leverage and cash-burn economics back at center stage despite $104.2B of Q2 backlog and more than $25B of additional early-Q3 commitments.

41. FLNC: Fluence's $2.9B backlog is no longer enough to offset execution risk; the key catalyst is proof that Houston manufacturing bottlenecks and delivery penalties are being resolved.

42. RARE: Ultragenyx now moves from regulatory risk to launch execution for Fayuvi, including treatment-center activation, reimbursement and initial patient uptake.

43. LCID: Lucid's Bolt partnership adds a second robotaxi commercialization path alongside its U.S. Uber/Nuro program, but timing and binding fleet orders remain critical.

44. HPK: HighPeak becomes an event-driven Permian name as elevated crude prices improve the strategic value of its 140,000-plus-acre position.

45. NKE: Nike's possible Dow removal creates an unusual index-composition catalyst on top of its existing turnaround challenge.

46. FED/OIL: The next equity move remains unusually sensitive to the combination of oil and the 10-year yield: Thursday's rally showed how quickly lower energy and duration pressure can re-rate growth stocks.

👉 DEEP ANALYSIS / MARKET INTELLIGENCE

47. AI POWER IS BECOMING A CONTRACTED REVENUE STORY: Generac's $2.4B initial Amazon order is more than half of its roughly $4.2B 2025 company revenue, while Crusoe now reports $140B-plus of contracted value and CoreWeave $104.2B of Q2 backlog. This suggests the AI infrastructure trade is migrating from speculative capex expectations into multi-year contractual obligations. The bottleneck is increasingly physical power, generators and energized capacity — not just GPUs.

48. COREWEAVE SHOWS THE OTHER SIDE OF THE AI CAPITAL CYCLE: CoreWeave has enormous demand visibility, but it is simultaneously raising $3B of convertibles and potentially another ~$2.9B through an ATM. Its contracted power rose to about 4.2 GW from 3.7 GW at June-end. The key read-through is that AI demand can be exceptional while equity economics remain financing-intensive; investors must separate revenue growth from per-share value creation.

49. GENERAC'S AMAZON WARRANT REVEALS HYPERSCALER BARGAINING POWER: Amazon can acquire up to 1.69M Generac shares, with most vesting tied to cumulative generator purchases up to $8B. This structure resembles strategic procurement deals where the customer captures part of the supplier upside it helps create. For investors, the warrant dilution is real, but it also signals Amazon expects the relationship could become much larger than the initial $2.4B.

50. FLUENCE IS A WARNING THAT BACKLOG WITHOUT THROUGHPUT CAN DESTROY VALUE: Fluence has roughly $2.9B of backlog yet cut FY2026 revenue to $2.4B and adjusted EBITDA to a ~$200M loss because manufacturing and logistics failed to convert demand into shipments. Compare that with Generac, which is explicitly tripling large-generator capacity into contracted demand. The capital-cycle lesson is simple: in infrastructure booms, manufacturing execution can matter more than order books.

51. LOWER YIELDS EXPLAINED MORE OF THURSDAY'S RALLY THAN A DOVISH FED: The Fed had just delivered its first hike in more than three years and markets still priced a 53.1% chance of another hike in October, yet the Nasdaq gained 1.69%. The 10-year yield slipping back below 5% and oil easing removed two immediate discount-rate shocks. This suggests equities can rally under tighter policy if the long end and energy complex stop tightening financial conditions independently.

52. TOKENIZATION JUST MOVED FROM CRYPTO NARRATIVE TO MARKET-STRUCTURE COMPETITION: The SEC's five-year exemption lets qualifying platforms trade real tokenized equities while preserving dividends and voting rights. Coinbase, Circle and Robinhood all rose more than 5%. One possible implication is that 24/7 settlement and self-custody become a competitive issue for traditional brokers and exchanges rather than merely a crypto-sector product feature.

53. LUCID'S ROBOTAXI STRATEGY IS SHIFTING THE EV MARGIN QUESTION: Bolt plans to own and operate at least 25,000 autonomous Lucid vehicles in Europe, while Lucid already has a U.S. program with Uber and Nuro. Fleet and autonomy economics could produce very different utilization and margin profiles from consumer EV sales. The important caveat is that the European agreement has no disclosed deployment timetable or binding vehicle order yet.

54. MARKET BREADTH CONFIRMED A REAL RISK-ON REVERSAL: Wednesday's Nasdaq session had far more decliners than advancers; Thursday flipped to 3,274 gainers versus 1,483 decliners while volume stayed above its 20-day average. Semiconductors rose more than 3% and tech led the S&P 500. This was not merely a mega-cap bounce — the breadth data show investors actively reversed part of the post-Fed de-risking.

text:
3/x

In Second Temple Jewish tradition and Christian theology, it became closely identified with Satan or demonic forces.
Modern academic scholarship often examines the term alongside Ancient Near Eastern motifs of divine serpents, chaotic monsters, and guardian beings (Seraphim, which also means "burning/fiery ones").

****

When modern scholars analyze these traits without the lens of the later "Satan" framework, they see a highly sophisticated blend of theological argument, rhetorical deconstruction, and ancient cultural motifs.

. "A Creation of God" (The Anti-Mythological Polemic)
The fact that Genesis explicitly calls the serpent a "beast of the field that the LORD God had made" is actually a massive theological statement by the ancient Hebrew authors.
In surrounding ancient cultures (like Mesopotamia, Egypt, and Canaan), serpents were often uncreated, eternal chaos monsters. For example, the Babylonian Tiamat or the Egyptian Apep were cosmic dragons that existed outside the creator god's authority and had to be violently subdued in epic battles.
By explicitly defining the nachash as a mere animal created by God, the author of Genesis strips the serpent of any divine or rival status. It isn't a dark god; it’s just a rogue creature. This establishes a strict monotheism where God has no true eternal rival.
2. "Most Crafty" (The Rhetorical Mastermind)
The Hebrew word used for crafty is 'arum. The serpent doesn't use magic or supernatural force to overpower Eve; it uses pure rhetorical strategy and formal logic. Scholars study the serpent's dialogue as a masterclass in deconstruction and structural fallacies:

The Straw Man

The Tactic: "Did God really say, 'You must not eat from any tree in the garden'?"

The Effect: Forces Eve to correct an exaggeration, drawing her into a debate and making her focus on the restriction rather than the garden's abundance.

The Direct Denial

The Tactic: "You will not certainly die."

The Effect: Directly contradicts the divine premise, introducing the possibility that the established rule is a lie.

The Red Herring (Motive)

The Tactic: "For God knows that when you eat from it your eyes will be opened..."

The Effect: Shifts the argument from the rule itself to the motive of the lawmaker, framing God as an insecure tyrant hoarding knowledge.

The "craftiness" of the serpent is its ability to weaponize human reason against divine command, making autonomy look logically superior to obedience.

3. Supernatural Speech (The Fable Motif)

Why does it talk? In the ancient world, animals crossing the boundary into human speech often signaled a breach in the cosmic order or functioned as a specific literary device.
The Fable Tradition: Just as animals speak in Aesop's fables or as Balaam's donkey speaks later in the Book of Numbers, talking animals were a recognized literary device in the ancient Near East. The talking serpent allows the author to personify temptation and autonomous human reasoning without requiring a complex metaphysical backstory (like a fallen angel).

The Threshold Guardian: In ancient folklore, talking animals often appear at thresholds or boundaries to test humans. The serpent stands at the boundary of divine wisdom (the Tree of Knowledge) and tests whether humanity is ready to wield it.

4. The Mesopotamian Thief (The Gilgamesh Parallel)
Scholars frequently connect the Genesis serpent to the Epic of Gilgamesh, a foundational text of ancient Mesopotamia.

In the climax of the Gilgamesh epic, the hero finally obtains a magical plant that restores youth and offers a form of immortality. While Gilgamesh is bathing, a snake smells the plant, sneaks up, and eats it. The snake immediately sheds its skin (symbolizing renewed life) and slithers away, leaving humanity to face inevitable death.

3/x ⬇️

text:
Rishikesh, India: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple 🛕 

Long ago, in the age when gods and demons roamed the heavens and the earth, a great event was about to take place — the Samudra Manthan, or the churning of the cosmic ocean of milk. The gods, led by Indra, and the demons, known as the Asuras, wanted to obtain Amrit, the nectar of immortality. To do this, they used Mount Mandara as the churning rod and the great serpent Vasuki as the rope, and together they churned the ocean.🌊 
As the ocean churned, many treasures appeared — divine gems, celestial beings, and miraculous plants. But along with the treasures came something dangerous: a deadly poison called Halahala. The poison was so powerful that its fumes threatened to destroy everything — the heavens, the earth, and even the oceans. The gods and sages were terrified. They ran to Lord Shiva, the supreme ascetic and protector of the universe, for help.🌻
Without hesitation, Lord Shiva decided to save the cosmos. He drank the poison, holding it in his throat. Its power was so strong that it burned his throat, turning it blue. From that moment, he became known as Neelkanth, the Blue-Throated One. Though he survived, the poison caused great pain and his body burned with its energy. To calm himself and meditate upon the balance of the universe, Shiva wandered through forests, mountains, and rivers, seeking a place of peace.✌️ 
During his journey, he reached the serene and lush hills near Rishikesh, where the Ganges flowed like a silver ribbonbetween the mountains. The air was filled with the sound of birds, rustling trees, and waterfalls. It was here, amidst the quiet majesty of nature, that Shiva chose to rest and meditate. The power of the poison gradually settled in his body as he focused his mind and practiced deep meditation, protecting the world while calming his own suffering.🕉️
Over time, people began to visit the spot where Lord Shiva had rested. They saw the mountain, the flowing river, and the waterfalls and felt the divine presence of the Lord. A temple was built on the hill, and it became known as the Neelkanth Mahadev Temple. Pilgrims from far and wide came to offer prayers, seeking the blessings of Shiva, who had sacrificed himself to save the universe. Even today, during the holy month of Shravan, thousands of devotees climb the hill and take the journey to this sacred site to honor the Blue-Throated Lord.🧿
The temple is not just a place of worship; it is a reminder of courage, selflessness, and devotion. Lord Shiva drank the poison to save all living beings, showing that true strength lies not in power but in sacrifice and protection of others. The Ganges flowing beside the temple, the surrounding forests, and the peaceful mountains make it a place where one feels the presence of the divine and the timeless story of Neelkanth come alive.🔱
Even today, visitors experience a sense of awe and reverence. Lighting lamps, offering flowers, and chanting mantras, they honor the Lord who bore the poison to preserve the world, understanding that his strength came from compassion and devotion. 🔱
Thus, the Neelkanth Mahadev Temple near Rishikeshstands as a living legend — a place where mountains, rivers, and devotion meet, where the sacrifice of Lord Shiva continues to inspire generations, and where every visitor is reminded of the power of courage, sacrifice, and divine grace.🌸

Jai Shree Neelkanth!! Har Har Mahadev!! Jai Bholenath ✨♥️🙏

text:
Chonburi Governor and Pattaya Mayor Join Ganesh Chaturthi Fire Aarti at Mahakali Temple in Pattaya

PATTAYA, September 17th, 2026 — Devotees packed the Mahakali Avatar Chakravala Chonnani Temple on Wednesday as local leaders joined a fire aarti ceremony marking Ganesh Chaturthi 2026.

The festival is being hosted by temple founder Amporn Kaewsaeng. Chonburi Governor Naris Niramaiwong presided over the rite, joined by Pattaya Mayor Poramese Ngamphiichet, Pattaya City Police Superintendent Pol. Col. Anek Srathongyu, Deputy Mayor Kritsana Boonsawat, Phanat Nikhom District Chief Chayapol Rattanawisuttikul, Chonburi Provincial Administrative Organization councillor Nakhon Phonluk-in, and other guests and worshippers.

Inside the temple, priests offered a fire aarti to Lord Ganesha and chanted hymns in accordance with Hindu tradition. Aarti, a ritual of worship with lamps or sacred fire, is a central part of Hindu deity veneration. Crowds continued to arrive throughout the day to pay respects and seek blessings.

Ganesh Chaturthi celebrates the birth of Lord Ganesha with prayers, offerings and aarti. The temple is holding events from Sept. 14 to 18.

On the evening of Sept. 17, the fire aarti was paired with performances by a singing troupe from India, adding color to the celebration. Today, Friday, September 18th, the final day, a morning aarti is scheduled before 11 a.m. The Ganesha image will then be carried in procession through the city to Bali Hai Pier in Pattaya for an immersion ceremony.

That closing rite, known as Visarjan, follows Hindu custom: at the end of the festival, the image of Lord Ganesha is taken to water and sent back to the divine realm, concluding this year’s observances.

text:
Imagine walking into an old bahay na bato in the middle of the afternoon.

Outside, the Philippine sun is almost blinding. But inside, daylight passes through hundreds of small, milky-white squares covering the windows. The room glows without the glare, creating the kind of soft, pearly light that has illuminated Filipino homes for generations.

That glow comes from capiz.

Long before modern glass became commonplace, Filipinos were already making remarkable use of the shell of the windowpane oyster, Placuna placenta.

Native to coastal and brackish waters across the Indo-Pacific, the oyster became particularly associated with the Philippines—and especially Capiz province in Panay, where it was historically abundant. Its remarkably flat, thin and translucent shell made it unlike most other mollusks.

Its story here stretches back centuries.

Before Spanish colonization, coastal communities were already harvesting shellfish for food and using shells for ornaments, tools and trade. But capiz would eventually find one of its most enduring purposes in colonial-era architecture.

Glass was expensive and difficult to obtain. Capiz offered a locally available alternative perfectly suited to the tropics.

Artisans cut the shells into small panes and fitted them into wooden latticework, creating the sliding windows that became a signature of the bahay na bato. They admitted daylight while diffusing its intensity and could be incorporated into large windows that helped ventilate homes.

Capiz became so closely associated with windows that an 1860 Tagalog-Spanish dictionary, Vocabulario de la lengua tagala, recorded “capiz” in connection with ventana—window.

Then glass became cheaper and easier to obtain.

Instead of disappearing, the craft adapted.

By the 20th century, Filipino artisans were transforming capiz into lampshades, chandeliers, trays, jewelry boxes, Christmas decorations and other decorative objects. Philippine capiz products eventually found buyers overseas, particularly during the export boom of the 1960s and 1970s.

But decades of harvesting, coastal degradation and changing consumer tastes took their toll.

Research on Philippine capiz fisheries documented serious declines caused by excessive harvesting, pollution, siltation and destructive fishing practices. A nationwide survey in the 1990s identified 27 natural capiz beds, with stocks already declining or depleted in many areas.

That is why today’s capiz revival begins not in a design showroom, but back in the sea.

Researchers have experimented with transplantation, hatchery production and restocking to rebuild populations rather than relying solely on wild harvests. Trials in Iloilo and Guimaras demonstrated the potential for growing and reproducing the oysters under managed conditions.

Conservation initiatives have also focused on rehabilitating Placuna placenta populations and protecting their habitats, alongside proposals for sanctuaries, community-based management and more sustainable harvesting.

Meanwhile, designers and researchers are finding new possibilities for the shell itself.

New biomaterial research is exploring how capiz scraps and manufacturing waste can be pulverized and reconstituted into usable materials, potentially giving pieces once destined for disposal another life.

The revival is cultural, too.

At a time when natural shells can be marketed internationally under vague or exoticized names, recognizing capiz as part of Philippine material culture matters. Behind every finished piece is not merely a pretty shell, but generations of knowledge about harvesting, cleaning, cutting, shaping and assembling an extraordinarily delicate natural material.

Capiz has already reinvented itself once—from food and ornament to windowpane, and from windowpane to global decorative craft.

Now it may have to reinvent itself again.

Because saving capiz is not simply about preserving the beautiful windows of ancestral houses. It means protecting the oyster in Philippine waters, sustaining the communities and artisans who work with it, and finding new uses that allow an old Filipino material to survive in a modern world.

Centuries after it first illuminated Filipino homes, capiz is looking for another chance to glow.

(✍️:Top Dagohoy)

text:
Interview with Gamecock freshman infielder, Miles Keogh:

•The Sarge Daily-
“What first got you into baseball, and when did you realize you wanted to play at the college level?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I first got into baseball because I wanted to play all the sports when younger. I think playing a lot of sports as I grew up helped a lot with my athleticism. I realized baseball was the one when I got to highschool and started to compete at the varsity level right away. I always knew I wanted to play one sport for as long as possible and was able to find that passion for baseball early in high school.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“Who has been the biggest influence on your baseball career?”

•Miles Keogh-
“Picking one influence on my basbeall career is so hard. I’d like to put that answer to my family and coaches. From learning from my older brother being able to play with him in high school to my parents always supporting the long summers and being there for me every time I’m off the field. My coaches in highschool who bought into my development made it easy for me to buy into them as well. My coaches have instilled confidence in me. I’ll have a lifelong relationship with them knowing I can always go to them when needed.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“When and how did you first connect with the coaching staff?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I first connected with the staff a little over a year ago over the phone. Those calls lead to them scouting me over the summer to eventually a visit at the end of the summer. As I was able to build a connection with Schnall and his staff I knew I was in the right hands and am excited to buy into them because I know they’re going to give me all they got as well.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“What are you most excited about regarding the team, facilities, or coaching staff?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I’m most excited to come up there and build a family with the team. I’m excited to get to college mature, grow, and get a lot better with what South Carolina has to offer.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“How do you see yourself fitting into the roster and contributing?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I see myself coming to South Carolina and making immediate impact having tools and being able to play multiple positions ready to give my teammates and coaches everything I got.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“What are your personal and team goals for your freshman year and beyond?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I want to play this game for as long as possible and ultimately give myself the best shot to be a big leaguer. There is a lot of small wins and personal goals that go along with that. I know everyone apart of South Carolina has a a championship goal in mind and it’s going to be a winning culture and I’m really excited to be apart of that.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“How do you mentally prepare for high-pressure situations or slumps?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I believe confidence comes from preparation. If I can go out on that field knowing I’ve done everything to prepare correctly for this moment then that’s all I can ask for and that’s where confidence comes from during the big plays.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“Favorite MLB player or team growing up, and why?”

•Miles Keogh-
“Arizona Diamondbacks. I enjoyed going to the park from a young age to now watching Ketel Marte and Geraldo Perdomo up the middle. They built some really cool chemistry.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“What’s a non-baseball hobby or interest you’re looking forward to pursuing in college?”

•Miles Keogh-
“I love the outdoors so being in South Carolina is perfect! I enjoy spending off time with teammates as well.”

•The Sarge Daily-
“Any advice for younger players going through the recruiting process?”

•Miles Keogh-
“Don’t rush it. Trust the process. Keep your head down and keep working. It will all fall in place as it should and enjoy every moment of it.”

BROADRIDGE $BR RAN $7.4 TRILLION THROUGH THE TECHNOLOGY THAT IS SUPPOSED TO REPLACE IT:

Broadridge Financial Solutions, ticker BR, at $164.31, -$2.78 / -1.66% today. Second of sixty-five on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5. The Lake Success, New York company is why a ballot arrives when a company you own holds its annual meeting.

Every name below is the one its Len5 watches without handing it the headline. The top name on a list is usually the one nobody argues with any more. The one behind it is where somebody still does.

The case against Broadridge has a name: tokenization. If share ownership sits on one shared digital ledger instead of passing along a chain of brokers and custodians, nobody needs a company in the middle keeping the records - which is why these shares sit 33.7% under the $247.64 they fetched last September 18.

The awkward part is that Broadridge runs one of those ledgers. Its Distributed Ledger Repo network processed $7.4 trillion of repo trades in August - short-term loans between big institutions secured by government bonds - and on September 2 it was widened to take G7 bonds.

The year ended June 30, reported August 4:

- Revenue $7,477M, +9%; $4,878M of it recurring revenue, the contracted part that arrives again next year
- Adjusted profit $9.60 a share, +12%; about 17 times that at today's price
- Dividend up 12% to $4.36 a year, a twentieth straight rise; 2.7% here

The number that decides it is closed sales - new business signed, which becomes recurring revenue later. On April 30 Broadridge cut its own forecast from $290M-$330M to $240M-$290M on longer sales cycles. The year finished at $305M, above the top of that cut range, and the year now running is guided back to $290M-$330M.

This Len5 wants settled earning power bought cheaply, and the disruption argument delivered the cheap half. CHANGE IT: the year now running is guided to 6% to 8% recurring revenue growth, and coming in under that is where clients leaving would show first. WHEN: November 3 before the open, tentative, $1.37 carried against $1.51. VERDICT: these shares jumped 7.0% to $168.41 on that report and closed under it today.

MOMENTUM LEN5:
Baldwin Insurance Group at $31.73 (after hours), -$0.31 / -0.97% today. Second of thirty. The Tampa company places insurance for businesses and families. This Len5 wants a price at its one-year high with both climbs agreeing, and a contract put it there on September 14: Sequence Holdings and DFO Management, Michael Dell's family office, agreed to buy it at $32.50 a share in cash, about $7.7B and some 88% above the June 17 close. What is left is 77 cents, 2.4%. CHANGE IT: only a rival bid clears $32.50. WHEN: November 3 after the close, tentative. VERDICT: a climb whose argument is now a merger agreement.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:
Comcast at $22.95 (after hours), -$0.78 / -3.29% today. Second of fifty-seven. The Philadelphia company sells Xfinity broadband. This Len5 wants a business almost nobody could rebuild, bought under its worth - here 7.7 times profit, on a 5.8% dividend. The rebuild half is argued by a price somebody else set: gigabit fiber at $30 to $40 a month, which finance chief Jason Armstrong called irrational on September 9. CHANGE IT: two straight quarters of shrinking broadband losses. WHEN: October 22 before the open, company-confirmed, $1.00 carried. GROWTH LEN5:
BOK Financial at $133.02, +$0.20 / +0.15% today. Second of thirty. The Tulsa bank lends to businesses across middle America. This Len5 wants profit growth the price has not already charged for: the June quarter, reported July 20, earned $2.92 a share against the $2.49 carried - little charged for at 12.5 times profit. The mix is unusual for a bank - $202M of fee income last quarter against $351.8M from lending. CHANGE IT: fee income is guided to the lower half of $820M-$845M, so the half that does not ride on rates has to stop slipping. WHEN: October 19 after the close, company-confirmed, $2.54 carried against $2.22. VERDICT: three quarters past expectations, and a lower price after all three.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:
Credo Technology at $167.36 (after hours), +$5.87 / +3.64% today. Second of thirty. Its 807 people design the chips and cables that move data between AI servers. This Len5 wants very fast growth on a base big enough to be real, and the quarter to August 1, reported September 1, carried both: revenue $479.0M, +115% on the year, a seventh straight quarter above 100%. CHANGE IT: growth landing under the 85% guided for this year. WHEN: November 30 after the close, tentative. VERDICT: the growth is not disputed - 57.6 times profit is, which is why these shares sit 45.8% under the $308.67 of June 22.

INCOME LEN5:
Ardmore Shipping at $19.00, -$0.06 / -0.32% today. Second of thirty. The Bermuda company runs 25 mid-size fuel and chemical tankers. This Len5 wants cash reaching owners that the business itself pays for. Nothing is fixed here: the policy hands over two thirds of each quarter's adjusted profit, doubled from one third in January - which is why the payment looks so large now. June quarter, reported July 29, earned $1.18 a share adjusted and paid $0.79 of it on September 15; the last four payments come to $1.37, about 7.2% of today's price. CHANGE IT: its tankers earned $51,870 a day in June and the September quarter is booked near $29,600. WHEN: November 4 before the open, tentative. Second place is not a consolation prize. It is where the disagreement still is. One of these six had its argument closed for it by a $7.7B cash offer; the other five answer for themselves between October 19 and November 30. text:
September 17th, 2026

Spotlight OTD: Steve Clifford 🎉🎂

For a coach who never got over the hump of winning a first-round playoff series, Steve Clifford sure does mean a lot to the history of this team.

I think of Clifford, and I immediately think of a few things: Stability when the Bobcats needed it maybe more than ever, defense, and probably Kemba Walker.  

Cliff certainly wasn’t perfect, but neither were any of his teams in Charlotte. He was a master at squeezing the most out of each group he had; his coaching career began in Charlotte after a buildup of 13 years for a job as the head coach.

A cool bit I found while researching: 

Searching for newspapers, I was looking through 2012 by mistake at the start. But, on May 2nd of 2012, almost a year and a month BEFORE Clifford was hired and the team was looking to replace Paul Silas, Rick Bonnell floated the idea of getting Clifford from Orlando as an option.

Charlotte ultimately hired Mike Dunlap, who only lasted one season before Clifford replaced him, and Bonnell mentioned later on that Dunlap had been a bit of a “cheap” move.

Clifford would proceed to lead Charlotte to the playoffs in his very first year as head coach. 

Despite a sweep to the Heat, going into Clifford’s second season in 2014-15, excitement was at the highest it’d been… since the team returned in ‘04? Steve coached Al Jefferson to an All-NBA Third Team, Kemba was coming into his own, and while the Gordon Hayward offer sheet was matched by Utah in 2014, the initial excitement about Lance Stephenson was pretty high.

‘14-‘15 ended up being a nightmare, but before the season, things were truly looking up. Charlotte didn’t re-sign Josh McRoberts, replaced him with Noah Vonleh who was a relative bust, Kemba and Al both spent some time injured, and Lance was… Lance.

Then came 2015-16, which was Clifford’s best with the Hornets. 

Just two years later in 2018 when Mitch Kupchak took over as GM, Steve Clifford was fired for the first time and eventually replaced by James Borrego… 

Only to infamously replace Borrego again four years later in 2022 after Borrego’s multiple play-in game disaster performances. 

Clifford would coach the Hornets for two more seasons after that before being replaced by Charles Lee himself in 2024 in the wake of MJ’s majority share sale to Gabe Plotkin and Rick Schnall. 

Clifford would remain on board with the Hornets as a front office member until just a few months ago when he went to join the Washington Wizards as a coaching advisor.

There were a lot of dud seasons in the middle for Steve, but you aren’t getting the full picture looking at it so simply like that. He was the first coach in 10 years — the sixth different Bobcats’ coach in TEN SEASONS — to calm the waters.

He was quite rigid with his defensive schemes at times, and wasn’t always the most adaptable, either… but he calmed the waters because he was consistent. 

Clifford was a great players’ coach, but also had the balance of having non-negotiables on court like his emphasis on defensive rebounding and limiting opponent points in transition.

Bonnell mentioned something incredibly interesting when Clifford got fired the first time, as well:

RB said outright that Malik Monk was the wrong draft selection over Donovan Mitchell, and had they selected Mitchell instead, Bonnell said “we’d be talking about playoff aspirations instead of a coaching search.”

I won’t disagree with that, and in a shell, that kind of sums up the totality of Clifford’s time here. They’d take a step forward, and unintentionally take one — or more sometimes — steps backwards. 

Bad drafts, misses in free agency outside of Al Jefferson… those things hinder a coach in the long run. Clifford never held a grudge, kept showing up to work each day and grinding regardless. He clearly had an immense respect for MJ as the owner despite his flaws.

text:
You can walk into a Catholic church almost anywhere on earth and know exactly where you are.

You could be in Rome, Poland, Kenya, Mexico, the Philippines, or sitting in a nearly empty parish in Chester County on a Tuesday morning. You may not understand a word being spoken, but you will still recognize the Mass. You will know when to stand, when to kneel, what is happening at the altar, and why everyone came.

That alone is incredible. But then you remember what it took for the Mass to survive.

It was offered in catacombs when Christians had to hide. It was offered in prison camps, during wars, in Irish homes when the faith was persecuted, and in underground churches where being caught could cost people everything. Priests risked their lives to celebrate it. Catholics risked theirs just to be there.

Kings died. Empires collapsed. Borders changed. Whole countries disappeared.

The Mass continued.

And now I get to walk into my church on an ordinary weekday morning and step into the same worship Catholics have carried across centuries.

That is what gets me.

Catholicism is not tied to one country, one culture, one preacher, or one generation. The Church is bigger than all of that.

You can cross an ocean, walk through the doors of a Catholic church, and still know exactly where you are.

Home.
